newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin to unveil new government plans on Friday.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin to unveil new government plans on Friday.

text.p: President Boris Yeltsin will sign an order on a new Russian government structure on Friday, Interfax news agency quoted the Kremlin leader as telling media editors.
Yeltsin said that the new government would be "cardinally different" from the previous one, though some of its members would keep their posts.
"The most important thing is that the people who will come will have new, fresh ideas and thoughts," Interfax quoted him as saying.
He added among the new cabinet members would be "people from the regions, those who have done well recently".

The wording used by Yeltsin did not make clear if he would announce the personnel line-up of the cabinet, being formed on his orders by Chernomyrdin and his first deputy Anatoly Chubais, or just the cabinet's structure.
Itar-Tass news agency quoted Yeltsin as saying the new government would include seven deputy prime ministers.
Yeltsin did not mention any names, apart from praising Communications Minister Vasily Bulgak.
The old government structure had three first deputies to Chernomyrdin and nine deputies. Yeltsin appointed liberal Chubais the one and only first deputy prime minister last Friday.

The number of deputy premiers appeared higher than indicated in previous leaks from the Kremlin, which made clear Chubais wanted a united team of allies at the top of the cabinet. This could mean that Yeltsin has decided to keep some of the older guard in the government.
